author: Mrkol
content:
<@132108381333880832> post-merge review for MapObjDolpic:
1) Lets avoid doing the _pad trick after all. Figuring out true inlines is more important than getting the number bigger
2) JGeometry::TVec3<f32> inherits from Vec, so you don't need explicit casts
3) Symbols like `up$2710` are generated for local static variables (static inside of a function), and the init thing is too
4) if you see dot products and cross products being used on 3 fields stored sequentially, that's probably a TVec3. You also had some (Vec*) casts of the fields to pass them to a function, so that's definitely a TVec3
5) the epsilon they usually use is JGeometry::TUtil<f32>::epsilon(), please use that rather than a hard-coded constant -- it influences codegen
6) TVec3::squared should be used for length squared
7) TVec3::operator-= exists, use it
8) Don't do C-style defining of all locals at the beginning of the function -- it's unlikely they did that
9) You can use inlines to change the order in which arguments are evaluated. MWCC quirk
10) Mtx* is almost never used, it's always MtxPtr. Ask for help if you have trouble wielding C's weird ass rules for arrays & pointers
11) In general, try to make the code feel more "normal", the original devs are not as crazy as I might make them out to be sometimes

Small question I'm curious about. Sometimes, objdiff shows me light blue mnemonics with an "original" in the tooltip. Is this because there is no separate opcode (is that the right word?) for cmplwi, so it just assembles to cmpli in this example? Or is there something else going on?
[attachment: image.png]

author: NickPlusPlus
content: PowerPC is a RISC ISA, so many of the opcodes have helper mnemonics that are more descriptive of what the actual operation is than the opcode can be

author: NickPlusPlus
content: This is more a result of the `cmplwi` op than it is to due with it being light blue. Light blue just means the original binary has the same opcode, but a different mnemonic/different arguments for the opcode

author: Mrkol
content: Oh, I think you want to drastically reduce the amount of temporaries you use. They influence the codegen heavily, and from what I've seen the devs really like just using stuff directly, without any intermediate temporaries

author: Mrkol

author: Mrkol
content:
<@156749888128811009> and others too. A lesson in decomp that I've learned in the last month: this codegen results from a && or || being assigned to a bool variable or being returned from an inline function. So sometimes it's not that they were doing these weird bool temporaries, but it's just that they've written something like `return thing && other_thing` 🙂
[attachment: image.png]

author: Mrkol
content: But in this case it might be a mix of both 🤔
